episodes.title: Case File: A Friend's File
sources: The Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964, Rule 3(1), clauses (xiii), (xv), (xvi), (xvii), as inserted by the CCS (Conduct) (Third) Amendment Rules, 2014 (DoPT notification, 27 November 2014); text read 2026-11-16 and re-checked 2026-11-19 from a reproduction at aaptaxlaw.com

Committee on Standards in Public Life (UK), The Seven Principles of Public Life (first set out by Lord Nolan in 1995); page read 2026-11-19 at https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-7-principles-of-public-life (origin of the principles only)
2nd ARC, Fourth Report, Ethics in Governance (2007), para 2.2.5; read 2026-11-19 at https://darpg.gov.in/sites/default/files/ethics4.pdf

quiz.q: What made Sameer's file hard for Ravi?
options: His senior ordered him to reject it
The land belonged to the state
quiz.why: The papers looked fine; the problem was the friendship, which no one else knew about.

quiz.q: What does a sound answer do with a conflict of interest?
options: Rejects the application to be safe
Keeps quiet if the papers are fine
Declares it and steps aside so merit decides
Approves it faster as a courtesy
quiz.why: Declaring and stepping aside protects both the public interest and the applicant's right to a fair decision.

quiz.q: Which rule asks a government servant to declare private interests relating to public duties?
quiz.why: Rule 3(1)(xiii), added in 2014, asks officers to declare private interests and resolve conflicts in the public interest.

episodes.title: Case File: The Gift Basket
sources: The Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964, Rule 13 (Gifts); read 2026-11-19 from reproductions at referencer.in and aaptaxlaw.com (not the Gazette)
CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, Rule 3(1)(xvi) (merit alone), as inserted by the CCS (Conduct) (Third) Amendment Rules, 2014
Committee on Standards in Public Life (UK), The Seven Principles of Public Life (Integrity), page read 2026-11-19 at gov.uk

quiz.q: Why is the contractor's basket a problem for Anita?
options: He has official dealings with her office
quiz.why: Rule 13 bars gifts, and the exceptions cover relatives and friends without official dealings, not a contractor whose bills she signs.

quiz.q: Why does sharing the basket around the office not solve it?
options: The gift was still accepted, and the contractor knows it
Sharing is illegal in every case
quiz.why: Passing it on spreads the sweets, not the obligation; the acceptance has already happened.

quiz.q: Which sound step does the case recommend?
options: Return it and record why in writing
Report the contractor to the police
quiz.why: Returning the gift and leaving a record follows the spirit of Rule 13, and the bills are still judged on merit alone.

episodes.title: Case File: The Report Nobody Wants
sources: The Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964, Rule 3(1)(i)-(iii); read 2026-11-19 from a reproduction at aaptaxlaw.com (not the Gazette)

Public Interest Disclosure and Protection of Informers (PIDPI) Resolution, 2004, as described in a Taxmann article (https://www.taxmann.com/post/blog/pidpi-whistleblowing-in-banks, read 2026-11-19): CVC as designated agency; identity protected
Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014: assent May 2014, not yet in force, per the same Taxmann article (read 2026-11-19)

quiz.q: Which Conduct Rules duties does quietly signing off break?
quiz.why: Rule 3(1)(i) and (ii) ask for absolute integrity and devotion to duty.

quiz.q: Since 2004, which body can receive complaints of misuse of office under a government resolution?
quiz.why: The PIDPI Resolution, 2004, makes the CVC the designated agency and protects the complainant's identity.

quiz.q: What is the status of the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014?
options: Has assent but is not yet in force
Struck down by the Supreme Court
quiz.why: It received the President's assent in May 2014 but has not been brought into force, as of the sources read.

episodes.title: Seven Principles of Public Life
sources: Committee on Standards in Public Life (UK), The Seven Principles of Public Life, page and text read 2026-11-19 at https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-7-principles-of-public-life (current descriptors; first set out by Lord Nolan in 1995)
2nd ARC, Fourth Report, Ethics in Governance (2007), para 2.2.5; read 2026-11-19 at https://darpg.gov.in/sites/default/files/ethics4.pdf

quiz.q: Which principle asks officials to declare and resolve any interests?
quiz.why: Integrity: avoid obligations to those who might influence you, and declare and resolve interests.

quiz.q: Which principle says information should be withheld only for clear and lawful reasons?
quiz.why: Openness asks for open and transparent decisions; information is withheld only for clear and lawful reasons.

quiz.q: Whose committee first set out the seven principles, and when?
quiz.why: The UK Committee on Standards in Public Life, under Lord Nolan, set them out in 1995.

episodes.title: Kautilya on the King's Happiness
sources: Kautilya's Arthashastra, tr. R. Shamasastry, 2nd ed. (Mysore, 1923), Book I, ch. 19; excerpt read 2026-11-19 at https://history.hanover.edu/courses/excerpts/261kaut.html
World History Encyclopedia, Arthashastra, https://www.worldhistory.org/Arthashastra/, read 2026-11-19 (rediscovery 1905, publication 1909, English translation 1915; authorship debated)

quiz.q: What does the Arthashastra say the king's happiness lies in?
quiz.why: Book I, ch. 19: in the happiness of his subjects lies his happiness; in their welfare his welfare.

quiz.q: What does the text say about petitioners at the court door?
options: They should be made to wait
The king should never make them wait
They should come once a month
quiz.why: A king who is inaccessible risks confusion, discontent and his enemies.

quiz.q: Who found the copy of the Arthashastra in 1905 and translated it into English in 1915?
quiz.why: R. Shamasastry found a copy in 1905, published it in 1909 and translated it in 1915.

episodes.title: Gandhi's Talisman
sources: Gandhi's "talisman", text as printed on "This Was Bapu", ch. 70 "The Gandhi Talisman", Gandhi Research Foundation / Bombay Sarvodaya Mandal, https://www.mkgandhi.org/thiswasbapu/70gandhitalisman.htm (read 2026-11-19; reproduction of the letter as recalled and transcribed)
Pyarelal, Mahatma Gandhi: The Last Phase, Vol. II (Navajivan, 1958): where the note is cited (named in the queue source hint; not re-read here)

quiz.q: Gandhi called the note he gave a friend tormented by doubts a what?
quiz.why: He wrote: "I will give you a talisman."

quiz.q: Which face does the talisman ask you to recall?
options: The poorest and most helpless man you have seen
quiz.why: "Recall the face of the poorest and the most helpless man whom you may have seen."

quiz.q: What should the step you contemplate give that person?
options: Control over his own life and destiny
quiz.why: The test asks whether the step will restore him to a control over his own life and destiny.

episodes.title: Chicago, 1893
sources: Swami Vivekananda, "Response to Welcome", The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, Vol. 1, Addresses at the Parliament of Religions (date 11 September 1893 as listed in the volume index), Wikisource, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Complete_Works_of_Swami_Vivekananda/Volume_1/Addresses_at_The_Parliament_of_Religions/Response_to_Welcome (read 2026-11-19; page flags the text as unverified against a scan)

quiz.q: On which date did Vivekananda give his "Response to Welcome" in Chicago?
quiz.why: The Complete Works list the Response to Welcome under 11 September 1893.

quiz.q: Which image did he use in the hymn he quoted?
options: Streams from different sources mingling in the sea
Many roads meeting at a city
quiz.why: "As the different streams having their sources in different places all mingle their water in the sea..."

quiz.q: What did he hope the morning bell would be the death-knell of?
quiz.why: He hoped the bell "may be the death-knell of all fanaticism".

episodes.title: Narayana Guru at Aruvippuram
sources: Kerala Tourism, "Aruvippuram Siva Temple" (Sree Narayana Guru section), https://www.keralatourism.org/sreenarayanaguru/temple-concept/aruvippuram-siva-temple (read 2026-11-19): consecration at midnight of Shivaratri 1888, the Neyyar river, 3 am, Kumaran Asan's tears, "We consecrated our Shiva", the reading of "we" and "our"; caste exclusion from major temples

Kerala Tourism, Sree Narayana Guru home page, https://www.keralatourism.org/sreenarayanaguru (read 2026-11-19): dates 20 August 1856 - 20 September 1928; Ezhava community; "One Caste, One Religion, One God for Humankind"

quiz.q: In which year did Narayana Guru consecrate the Shiva stone at Aruvippuram?
quiz.why: The first phase of his consecrations began with Aruvippuram in 1888.

quiz.q: What was his reported reply to those who questioned the act?
quiz.why: The words "we" and "our" are read as a declaration of equality and love.

quiz.q: Which message is associated with Narayana Guru?
options: One caste, one religion, one God for humankind
quiz.why: "One Caste, One Religion, One God for Humankind" is his best-known message.

episodes.title: The Blind Men and the Elephant
sources: Udana 6.4 (Tittha Sutta: Sectarians (1)), tr. John D. Ireland, The Udana: Inspired Utterances of the Buddha (Kandy: Buddhist Publication Society, 1997), https://www.accesstoinsight.org/tipitaka/kn/ud/ud.6.04.irel.html (read 2026-11-19); the story, the nine parts and their comparisons are retold in our own words

quiz.q: In which Buddhist text does the story of the blind men and the elephant appear?
quiz.why: It is in Udana 6.4 (the Tittha Sutta).

quiz.q: What did the man who felt the elephant's head say it was like?
quiz.why: Head: a water jar; ear: a winnowing basket; tusk: a plowshare.

quiz.q: What does the tale teach about a single viewpoint?
options: It is only one side of things
quiz.why: Those who see only one side of things end up quarrelling.

episodes.title: Two Sides: Do Ends Justify Means?
sources: J. S. Mill, Utilitarianism (1863), ch. 2, 'What Utilitarianism Is': 'actions are right in proportion as they tend to promote happiness', read at marxists.org 2026-11-19

I. Kant, Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals (1785), second section (Academy ed. 4:429), the formula of humanity (never merely as a means); as discussed in Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Treating Persons as Means', read 2026-11-19 (secondary)
M. K. Gandhi, Hind Swaraj (1909; English 'Indian Home Rule'), ch. XVI 'Brute-Force': means as a seed, the end as a tree, archive.org full text, read 2026-11-19

quiz.q: Which writer, in 1863, said actions are right as they tend to promote happiness?
quiz.why: John Stuart Mill, in Utilitarianism (1863), judged actions by their tendency to promote happiness.

quiz.q: In Hind Swaraj, how does Gandhi picture the link between means and end?
options: A coin and its two faces
quiz.why: He wrote that the means are like a seed and the end like a tree, with an unbroken connection between them.

quiz.q: In a Mains answer on a question like this, what is the sound approach?
options: Pick one thinker and dismiss the rest
Set out both views with a thinker for each, then a balanced way forward
quiz.why: The video's takeaway: both views, fairly, each with a thinker, then a balanced way forward.
